clue.text: Disillusion sailor surrounded by neglect

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside the other word, so the sailor goes within the neglect

parts.note: disuse is the state of being neglected or left unused
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword's standard sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor left to rot in neglect would certainly lose his illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neglect' reads as part of the sailor's story, but it is the outer word that wraps around him.
explanation.definitionFit: To disabuse someone is to free them from a mistaken belief, which is exactly what disillusioning them does.

clue.text: Daughter admitted being drunk

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to own up is to admit, so owned means admitted

explanation.surface: A daughter confesses to being intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as intoxicated, but it is the past participle of drink: consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint that has been downed has been swallowed quickly, so downed and drunk are both past participles of consuming a beverage.

clue.text: Heads to slay King Edward with enormous rolling pin

indicators.note: heads are the front ends, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.words: slay King Edward with enormous rolling
parts.note: the opening letters of six consecutive words

explanation.surface: A grim kitchen tale of killing a king with a giant rolling pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling pin' looks like one kitchen tool; 'rolling' is fodder and 'pin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long thin metal or wooden spike used to hold meat together, a kind of pin.

clue.text: Stern about left showing return to old habits

indicators.note: about means around, so the stern wraps around the single letter for left

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a boat, and one's backside is one's rear
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A ship's stern swinging to port suggests a vessel drifting back where it came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad old ways after a period of improvement.

clue.text: Overpriced contract to include church in cross-country race

parts.note: a steep price is an excessive one

indicators.note: a contract that includes something holds it within its terms, so the church sits inside

parts.note: a lease is a rental contract
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An expensive deal to put a church on the route of a country race.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race across country with fences and ditches, originally run from one church steeple to another.

clue.text: Look around terraces in outskirts of Basingstoke

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the terraces go inside
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters of the place name count

parts.note: first and last letters of the town's name
terraces are rows of houses

explanation.surface: A visitor wanders past the terraced streets on the edge of Basingstoke, a town in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look around casually, as in a shop, without a fixed purpose.

clue.text: Almost sit in gum

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to sit is to rest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly sitting in some chewing gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance exuded by trees, and gum is another name for such plant secretions.

clue.text: Story with house deserted initially by one

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A tale of a house deserted at first by one inhabitant, like the opening of a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective novel or play centred on solving a murder, so a kind of story.

clue.text: Antagonise wayward sergeant

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the proper course, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly sergeant is told to provoke someone, or perhaps his behaviour provokes everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them hostile or unfriendly, alienating them, which is close to antagonising.

clue.text: Miserable wife gagged

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to gag is to heave as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: A wife who has just gagged is understandably feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched describes someone in a deeply unhappy or pitiable state, a close synonym of miserable.

clue.text: Accompany old car

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go along with someone as a guide or guard
second meaning: a Ford model sold in Britain from the 1960s to 2000

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to ride along in a vintage motor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Escort was one of Britain's best-selling family cars, now discontinued.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to go with someone; as a noun it names a discontinued Ford hatchback model.

clue.text: Determined to keep trick unpredictable

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold onto it, so the trick is held inside

parts.note: an insistent person is determined to have their way
a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A con artist determined to keep their tricks unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconsistent behaves erratically and does not follow a steady pattern, so it cannot be predicted.

clue.text: Bookies never returned to cover bet

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left
the words cover the answer, which lies inside them across the word break

parts.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Bookmakers who never give money back still have to cover the bets placed with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a betting price where the stake is matched one for one, so a wager at that price is called an evens bet.

clue.text: Alpine sun melted strip of land

indicators.note: something melted loses its shape and can be remoulded, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mountain sunshine has melted the snow off a narrow piece of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is a narrow piece of land jutting into water, surrounded by sea on three sides.

clue.text: Bird living in lodgings for sport

parts.note: the kite is a bird of prey
a boarder lives in lodgings, paying for room and meals

explanation.surface: A bird nesting in someone's lodgings makes an odd kind of hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiteboarding is a water sport in which a rider on a board is pulled along by a large kite.

clue.text: Put off holding stick when rising in repeated performance

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle; the phrase describes something done again in performance

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top
holding means keeping in one's grasp, so the stick goes inside the first word

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: An actor put off by being handed a walking stick during a repeat show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reenacted is performed again, as a historical battle is restaged by enthusiasts.

clue.text: Insulating material, like top of seals' heads

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
to top is to best, outdo

indicators.note: heads are the front ends, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Seals' heads are well insulated by blubber, perhaps like a lagging material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used to insulate buildings against heat and fire.

clue.text: Bend track for flyer

parts.note: to warp is to bend out of shape
a lane is a narrow track or road

explanation.surface: A curve in the running track suits a sprinter, a 'flyer' on the athletics field.
explanation.definitionFit: A warplane is a military aircraft, and a flyer here means something that flies.

clue.text: Disgruntled whip's rage set aside

indicators.note: disgruntled means put out of humour, suggesting the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A party whip, the MP who enforces voting discipline, finally sets aside his fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' reads as one phrase; 'set' is fodder and 'aside' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre an aside is a remark meant for the audience, delivered as a loud whisper the other characters supposedly cannot hear.

clue.text: Hard atmosphere at party in Barnet

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the air is the atmosphere around us
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A tense mood at a party held in Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is cockney rhyming slang for hair, from Barnet Fair; capitalised it poses as the London place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a styled arrangement of the hair, which rhyming slang calls one's barnet.

clue.text: Count caught us hiding three bridge players

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it out of sight inside itself

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
East, North and South are three of the four seats at a bridge table

explanation.surface: A tally that catches us concealing three card players at a bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population, so the noun names a count.

clue.text: Repossess frothy coffees

indicators.note: a frothy liquid has been whipped up and agitated, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bailiffs come to take back the frothy coffees, perhaps from a café that cannot pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frothy' looks like a description of the coffees but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Espressos are strong coffees made by forcing steam through finely ground beans.

clue.text: Air film with that woman

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: A woman airs a film she has made.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a poetic word for the upper air or the clear sky.

clue.text: Humble home with acre in front

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acre
a base is where one lives or works from

explanation.surface: A modest house with an acre of land at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front' places the acre's letter before the home.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase is to lower someone in dignity or esteem, the verb sense of humbling them.

clue.text: Worthless attempt to cover up remains

indicators.note: covering something up means wrapping it, so the attempt goes around the remains

parts.note: a try is an attempt
ash is what remains after burning, as in cremated remains

explanation.surface: A feeble effort to hide the evidence that turns out to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy means cheap and of poor quality, close to rubbish, hence of little value.

clue.text: Teeth make an impression on your outspoken son

parts.note: a dent is a physical impression in a surface

indicators.note: outspoken taken literally means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: said in a clipped accent, the possessive is close to this spelling
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone's blunt-talking son is told to bite into something hard enough to leave a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: 'your' must be heard as the ending of 'dentures'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are a set of false teeth, so the plural noun stands in directly for teeth.

clue.text: Blackens small and medium corncobs

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing labels
an ear of corn is a cob

explanation.surface: Corn on the cob, small and medium sizes, is charred black on a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear someone is to blacken their name with slander; both verbs mean damaging a reputation.

clue.text: Hard-working boss promises to pay back money

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
an IOU is a written note promising to repay a debt

explanation.surface: An employer hands out written promises to repay borrowed cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer, but here it is the ornamental knob on a shield or ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person applies themselves diligently to study, so the adjective means hard-working in learning.
